evidence.source: Ctext, received text of Shuowen Jiezi
evidence.field: 兒 entry; 說文解字, 儿部
evidence.text: The entry glosses 兒 as a young child and says its form follows 儿, depicting a child whose fontanel has not closed. This is a historical dictionary explanation, not independent proof of the depicted anatomy.
evidence.title: 說文解字 : 卷九 : 儿部

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, 說文解字 entry for 兒
evidence.field: Duan Yucai commentary; graphic interpretation and extension
evidence.text: Duan explains the seal form’s upper 臼-like shape as the infant’s unclosed cranial fontanel and glosses the word’s extension as young or small generally. This preserves the received account, not independent confirmation of the image interpretation.
evidence.title: 說文解字「兒」

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文 transcriptions, graphic description, readings, and cited usage
evidence.text: The entry reports a textual difference: the Great Xu edition transcribes the component as 几, while Duan’s edition has 儿. It describes the regular-script upper part as 臼-like and associated with the fontanel, with 儿 below. It gives readings ér for child-related senses and ní for a surname equivalent to 倪. Its examples include a child-address use in a Han-attributed poem (with the caveat that this is a textual attribution), parental address/self-reference, a young-man sense, an insult, and suffixal uses in later works. The examples attest usages in those cited texts but do not establish the first occurrence or a complete chronology of the semantic links.
evidence.title: [A00277] 兒 - Ministry of Education 《Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants》

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, 漢語多功能字庫
evidence.field: 甲金文 shape analysis and disputed interpretation
evidence.text: The account describes early forms as combining a person-like element with a 臼-like element. It reports two interpretations of the latter: an unclosed infant skull/fontanel, following Shuowen, or a child’s paired hair-buns. It identifies the original sense as child. The source presents the depicted feature as disputed; this evidence does not settle which interpretation is correct.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：兒

evidence.field: modern readings and dictionary gloss inventory
evidence.text: The entry gives readings including ér and ní and lists senses such as child, son, address to a younger person, young man, self-reference, suffix, and weak/small. A gloss inventory alone does not establish their relative dates or semantic development.
evidence.title: 漢字「兒」：基本資料

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 兒/儿 distinction and variant evidence
evidence.text: The dictionary treats 儿 as a simplification of 兒 in one account, while distinguishing the historical Shuowen component 儿 from the character form meaning child. Its discussion of traditional forms and readings does not make 儿 a phonetic component of 兒.
evidence.title: [A00277-002] 儿 (兒) - Ministry of Education 《Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants》

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Xiaoxuetang Character Form Evolution Database
evidence.text: The official Xiaoxuetang service describes a database of forms with source and form-analysis information. The supplied public search pages expose the query interface but this search did not yield a specific 兒 record with a selectable rendered glyph URL. The project’s rights notice is reported in the supplied research instructions, but I did not inspect an official notice page during this search and therefore do not propose a Xiaoxuetang image.
evidence.title: 小學堂字形演變

gaps: No suitable direct glyph image URL with verified identity and reuse rights was established. Generic oracle-bone artifacts and Commons glyphs for other characters were excluded; no historical glyph candidates are proposed.

The exact depicted feature in early 兒 forms remains disputed: Shuowen and Duan’s commentary identify an unclosed fontanel, while the CUHK account also reports a topknot interpretation. The inspected accessible text does not resolve the dispute.

The dossier and pages inspected do not securely date the earliest semantic use of the spoken child word. A Han-attributed poem supplies a textual example, but attribution and transmission do not establish a contemporary dated witness.

The semantic chronology from child to son, forms of address/self-reference, young man, insult, and grammatical suffix remains undetermined; dictionary example lists do not establish the links or first dates.

No sound component is proposed for 兒. Its infant graph is analyzed pictographically; 儿 is discussed as a shape/component, not as a phonetic element. No component origin_relation classification is applicable.
The search did not establish an exact formal promulgation date for the simplified form 儿.

limitations.text: Searches found no exact, source-described 兒 image with independently verified direct image URL and reuse permission. Xiaoxuetang was considered, but the query yielded no exact record image URL; unrelated Commons glyphs and generic artifact photographs were not selected.

Early forms are discussed in the inspected dictionaries, but no glyph pixels were visually inspected in this research stage. The fontanel versus paired-hair-bun interpretation remains unresolved in the accessible descriptions.
